s: A company runs an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL global database. The primary cluster is in us-east-1 and a secondary cluster is in eu-west-1. Twice a year, the company must run a DR test by moving write traffic to eu-west-1 for one week and then moving it back. No committed transactions can be lost during the test. The application connects through the global database writer endpoint. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational effort?
o: Use an Aurora global database switchover to make the eu-west-1 cluster the primary. After the test, perform another switchover back to us-east-1.
Use an Aurora global database managed failover to promote the eu-west-1 cluster. After the test, use a managed failover back to us-east-1.
Detach the eu-west-1 cluster from the global database to promote it to a standalone cluster. After the test, rebuild the global database from us-east-1.
Take a manual snapshot of the primary cluster, copy it to eu-west-1, and restore it. After the test, copy the changes back with AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS).

w.y: A switchover (formerly 'managed planned failover') is the planned operation: Aurora waits until the secondary is fully synchronized before swapping roles, so RPO is 0, and the global topology stays intact for the move back. The global writer endpoint follows the new primary, so the application needs no change.

o.A: Correct. Planned, no data loss, topology preserved, endpoint follows automatically.
o.B: Failover is for unplanned outages. It promotes the secondary without waiting for synchronization, so committed transactions that had not replicated yet can be lost.
o.C: Detaching breaks replication and the global database must be rebuilt afterwards. Writes made in the gap can be lost and the effort is high.
o.D: A snapshot and restore loses every write made after the snapshot, and copying changes back with DMS is slow and error-prone.

s: Aurora Global Database switchover and failover
